diagnostic_evidence.quote: The union of the disjoint sets $L_{\bsl(u,\bsk')}$ over all $\bsk' \le \bsk$ covers exactly the set of all Walsh indices $\bs h$ where $h_j < b^{k_j+1}$ for all $j \in u$ and $h_j=0$ for $j \notin u$. This corresponds precisely to the index set we previously denoted as $\tilde{L}_{\bsl(u,\bsk),u}$.
L_{\bsl} = \{ \bsh = (h_1,\dots,h_d) \in \NN_0^d \mid b^{l_j-1} \le h_j < b^{l_j} \text{ if } l_j>0, \text{ and } h_j=0 \text{ if } l_j=0 \}

issues.failure_explanation: The identity equates the sum of ANOVA components beta_{u,k'} over k'<=k with the local average tilde-beta_{u,u,k}. Via the Walsh representation (Appendix), the left side covers the union of index sets L_{l(u,k')} over k'<=k. Each such L has l_j = k'_j+1 >= 1 for j in u, so it requires h_j >= b^{l_j-1} >= 1 and therefore never contains h = 0. The right side tilde-beta_{u,u,k} is the Walsh sum over L-tilde_{l(u,k),u} which does include h = 0, contributing hat{f}(0) = f_emptyset. Consequently the correct identity is sum = tilde-beta minus f_emptyset (for u nonempty), and the Appendix claim that the union of L sets equals L-tilde is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the term -f_emptyset to the right-hand side of eq:beta2 and correct the Appendix proof by observing that the union of L_{l(u,k')} over k'<=k omits h = 0 from L-tilde. Lemma lem:beta-basechange and all downstream results remain valid.
issues.overall_effect: The stated identity eq:beta2 and its Appendix proof are incorrect. No downstream formal result is invalidated because the f_emptyset discrepancy cancels in the inclusion-exclusion inside Lemma lem:beta-basechange (the sum over v of (-1)^{|u|-|v|} vanishes for |u| >= 1), and all other results use only properties that remain established.
issues.title: ANOVA identity eq:beta2 is false: missing constant term
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local correction (adding one term and fixing one proof sentence). Every substantive claim and guarantee is preserved with no new lemma, construction, or replacement argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: C_{u,v,\bsk}(P_n) = \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{i'=0}^{n-1} \chi(\text{$\bsx_i$ and $\bsx_{i'}$ are in the same elementary $(\bsk + \bsone_v)$-interval})

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the product in eq:Gtilda_def yields G-tilde = (1/n) * sum-sum prod = n * sum_v H_{u,v} C_{u,v,k} when C is normalized with 1/n^2 as in eq:C_def. But eq:Gtilda_formula states G-tilde = sum_v H_{u,v} C_{u,v,k} without the factor n. The three equations eq:Gtilda_def, eq:C_def, and eq:Gtilda_formula are mutually inconsistent. As a consequence the defined G is 1/n times the standard gain coefficient. For example with d=1, u={1}, k_1=1, b=2, n=2 and points x_0=0, x_1=1/2 in distinct k-intervals the stated definitions give G=1/2, contradicting Theorem thm:mimic item (i) which asserts G=1 for n <= m_{u,empty,k}=2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the extra 1/n normalization factor from eq:G_Gtilde (or equivalently from eq:Gtilda_def) and adjust eq:C_def and eq:Gtilda_formula to the consistent convention in which G = (1/(n*prod(b_j-1))) * sum-sum prod. All stated results then hold with the standard normalization.
issues.overall_effect: Every gain-coefficient value is understated by a factor 1/n. The variance formula eq:variance-gain returns Var_true/n instead of Var_true. Theorem thm:mimic items (i), (iii), (iv), (v) are incorrect as stated. Corollary cor:gain-0ed exact-value assertions (G=1 at n=b^m) and Corollary cor:maxgain_uk (max G = Gamma_u) fail. Bounds in cor:added-2 and the rate claim in cor:added-4 survive because the 1/n discrepancy cancels in the final inequalities.
issues.title: Gain-coefficient normalization inconsistent across definitions and formulas
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine normalization adjustment (changing prefactors in two or three equations). Every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee survives; no new lemma, construction, or argument is needed.
